title: Characterize the face/h-vectors of simple or simplicial convex polytopes
statement: Determine which integer h-vectors arise from simplicial convex polytopes, equivalently from their simple polar duals. The g-theorem imposes h-symmetry and the Macaulay M-sequence condition on successive differences.
status: E: solved before the talk by Billera--Lee sufficiency and Stanley necessity; the two contributions are complementary.

title: Density of finite-critical-orbit quadratic parameters: ambient set unspecified
statement: The notebook asks whether parameters \(c\) for which the critical orbit of \(z^2+c\) is finite are dense, without an unambiguous ambient set.
status: F: the whole-plane interpretation is false because |c|>2 is an open escape region. The intended restricted formulation is unidentified, and no density-of-hyperbolicity conjecture is substituted.

title: A rigorous operator-family framework for the anomaly sign
statement: Editorial specialization of Gelfand's broad request: construct determinant/Pfaffian lines for elliptic families, gauge-compatible transport, and a spectral formula for mapping-torus holonomy.
status: B: later determinant-line and eta-invariant theory supplies a rigorous substantial answer to this specialization; the undefined general field-theory program is not claimed solved.

title: Transition matrices and multiplication rules for standard symmetric functions
statement: Determine the change-of-basis matrices among \(m_\lambda,e_\lambda,h_\lambda,p_\lambda,s_\lambda\), and the Schur multiplication coefficients, degree by degree.
status: E: classical formulas available before1983; exact matrix-counting and tableau rules verified in the cited reference.

title: Compute the normalized formal wave coefficients recursively
statement: For a normalized scalar operator \(L_n\), recursively determine the coefficients of \(\Psi=e^{kx}(1+\sum_{r\ge1}c_rk^{-r})\) in \(L_n\Psi=k^n\Psi\), specifying integration constants.
status: E: the formal recursive construction was established before1983; the n=2 recurrence is supplied and its first coefficients checked.

title: Verify the complete-symmetric-function generating product
statement: Show that \(\sum_{r\ge0}h_rt^r=\prod_i(1-tx_i)^{-1}\) as a formal series in the graded symmetric-function ring.
status: E: elementary exercise resolved by expanding each geometric-series factor and counting variable multiplicities.

title: Find the width of the rectangular partition poset
statement: For diagrams in an \(m\)-by-\(n\) rectangle ordered by inclusion, determine the largest number of pairwise incomparable diagrams.
status: E: Stanley's pre1983 hard-Lefschetz/Sperner theorem identifies the width with the middle Gaussian-binomial coefficient and proves the strong Sperner property.

title: Recursive odd-order KdV Lax operators (earlier stable problem)
statement: For \(L=\partial^2+u\), construct the odd differential parts \((L^{(2r+1)/2})_+\) and the associated KdV Lax flows. The1983 occurrence treats a broader scalar order n and links only through this n=2 specialization.
status: E: established formal pseudodifferential construction. Earlier identifier reused for the exact KdV specialization; earlier cumulative occurrence history must be retained when merging.

notes: The seminar asks for a direct explanation of the equal rank classes underlying the partition congruences.
statement: For $m=5$ with $n=5q+4$, and for $m=7$ with $n=7q+5$, seek a uniform direct operation on Young diagrams partitioning n that gives an m-cycle action and increases Dyson rank modulo m by 1. The rank is largest part minus number of parts. A construction obtained by separately enumerating each finite rank class and matching their enumeration indices is excluded from the intended combinatorial explanation.
reconstruction: Atkin--Swinnerton-Dyer equidistribution already implies that finite bijections exist. Consequently the bare existential statement is E, whereas the historical request for a direct diagram operation is the substantive combinatorial question. The word direct encodes an intended form of explanation rather than a newly proved complexity lower bound.
fate: The opened Atkin--Swinnerton-Dyer publisher record and the checked theorem identification establish the equidistribution background. Stanton (2019), section 3 of Some Problems and OPAC-001, explicitly asks for the rank-class bijections/cyclic constructions. The targeted searches found no later verified solution, but this is a bounded literature-status claim. \citep{atkinswinnertondyer1954partitions,stanton2019problems,stanton2019rankcrank}.
present_status: Status as of 12 November 2026: C for the intended direct combinatorial construction, with an explicit opened open-problem source from 2019; no claim that every later publication has been exhaustively checked.
literal_correctness: Correct as a request for a direct combinatorial explanation; abstract finite-set existence is already settled.
worth: A meaningful open combinatorial direction. The negative-coefficient obstruction for one rank-polynomial route is already in Stanton and is not a new result of this companion.

notes: The asymptotic size of the largest irreducible representation of the symmetric group is questioned.
statement: Let $d_n=\max_{\lambda\vdash n}f^\lambda$ and $a_n=-n^{-1/2}\log(d_n/\sqrt{n!})$. Determine the limiting exponent and its value. Aggarwal--Elboim Theorem 1 establishes a constant $d>0$ such that $|a_n-d|\leq C/\log n$ for sufficiently large n. An explicit evaluation of d and stronger asymptotics are separate questions not answered by that theorem.
reconstruction: The Plancherel identity gives the leading square-root-factorial scale, while maximal and typical diagram dimensions must not be conflated. Earlier upper/lower bounds do not prove convergence. The 2026 theorem changes the answer to the limit-existence part of the notebook question.
fate: Vershik--Kerov (1985), section 1, Theorems 1--2, gives bounds and discusses the limit issue. The opened Aggarwal--Elboim preprint, first posted 25 May 2026, Theorem 1 on page 2, proves convergence with the stated logarithmic error. No journal publication was verified, and the paper does not explicitly evaluate d. \citep{vershikkerov1985dimensions,aggarwalelboim2026maximal}.
present_status: Status as of 12 November 2026: the convergence component has a 2026 preprint theorem; the retained C assessment concerns the explicit constant and stronger asymptotic information. Preprint theorem status is distinguished from peer-reviewed publication.
literal_correctness: The question is meaningful after fixing the normalization; claims of unresolved convergence must be updated to the 2026 theorem.
worth: Potentially valuable for precise evaluation or sharper asymptotics. Numerical fits and conditional dimension bounds do not prove the constant and are not advertised as a solution.

status: Status as of 12 November 2026: the convergence component has a 2026 preprint theorem; the retained C assessment concerns the explicit constant and stronger asymptotic information. Preprint theorem status is distinguished from peer-reviewed publication.

notes: The positive cone is asked for after the symmetric-function realization of the K-functor.
statement: For the Young-graph dimension group, identify the underlying ordered group with $\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}/(s_{(1)}-1)$. To test positivity, first represent a class by a homogeneous symmetric function f, homogenizing terms with powers of $s_{(1)}$ if necessary. The class is positive if and only if $s_{(1)}^k f$ is a nonnegative integral linear combination of Schur functions for some $k\geq0$.
reconstruction: Homogenization is essential: an arbitrary inhomogeneous representative such as s\_(1)-1 represents zero but does not become Schur-positive merely by multiplying all terms by one common power. At a fixed homogeneous level, the transition map is multiplication by s\_(1), and the inductive-limit positive cone is the union of the images of the finite-level nonnegative cones.
fate: Vershik--Kerov (1983), section 6.1 and the discussion in section 6.7, gives the symmetric-function K-functor/positive-cone description in the same year and before this seminar record. The opened primary text was read. This is an established structural answer, not a still-open positivity problem. \citep{vershikkerov1983kfunctor}.
present_status: Status as of 12 November 2026: E for the reconstructed ordered-group statement.
literal_correctness: Correct with the finite-level homogeneous representative and eventual positivity made explicit.
worth: Useful precise annotation and historical cross-reference; no new open question is created.
title: The ordered K-group and eventual Schur positivity
scope: The positive cone in the symmetric-function description of the Young-graph dimension group.
status: Status as of 12 November 2026: E for the reconstructed ordered-group statement.

notes: The problem of finding eigenfunctions of a one-dimensional many-particle Hamiltonian is posed.
statement: For fixed N, circle length $\ell>0$ and real c, consider $H_N=-\sum_{j=1}^N\partial_{x_j}^2+2c\sum_{i<j}\delta(x_i-x_j)$ on wavefunctions in $L^2((\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z)^N;(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N})$ antisymmetric under simultaneous coordinate-spin exchange. Define the operator by its closed semibounded contact-interaction quadratic form, equivalently continuity and the contact derivative jump. Seek its energies and wavefunctions in fixed particle-number and spin sectors.
reconstruction: The kinetic energy has a minus sign. Repulsive c>0 and attractive c<0 require different root configurations; on the line rather than a circle the spectral statement includes continuous-spectrum generalized eigenfunctions.
fate: Yang 1967 gives the repulsive spinful Bethe construction before this lecture. Equations1--12 and20--27 were read. His footnote1 does not prove full completeness in every sector, so E applies to the established solution method and explicit eigenpair construction, not an unqualified modern completeness theorem. \citep{yang1967manybody,yang1968smatrix}.
present_status: Status as of 12 November 2026: the reconstructed result is established; the cited verification has the limits stated below.
literal_correctness: The written kinetic sign is wrong for the intended positive kinetic energy; boundary conditions must be fixed.
worth: Established integrable model; clarify domain and completeness rather than manufacture a new open problem.

status: Status as of 12 November 2026: the reconstructed result is established; the cited verification has the limits stated below.

notes: The three-dimensional analogue of the Yang--Baxter equation is displayed, and the existence of nontrivial solutions is questioned.
statement: A constant tetrahedron equation for $R\in\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes3})$ is $R_{123}R_{145}R_{246}R_{356}=R_{356}R_{246}R_{145}R_{123}$ on $V^{\otimes6}$; spectral-parameter versions require a specified compatible parameter assignment. In the broad sense of a nontrivial solution, existence was already established before the 12 December 1983 lecture.
reconstruction: Zamolodchikov proposed nontrivial solutions in 1981, and Baxter proved their validity in a paper published in June 1983. A narrower request involving a particular finite dimension, positivity, parameter dependence or classical limit cannot be supplied from the fragment. Later q-oscillator constructions use appropriate algebraic Fock spaces and restrictions on q; they are not interchangeable with every possible finite-dimensional requirement.
fate: Baxter (1983) was received on 28 October 1982 and published in June 1983. Its opened publisher abstract explicitly states the proof of Zamolodchikov solutions, so the broad existence question is E. The full Baxter proof was not read. Bazhanov--Sergeev (2005 preprint; 2006 article), section 4, equations 27--33, was read for a later explicit construction. This corrects the earlier provisional attribution of the fate solely to that later construction. \citep{zamolodchikov1981tetrahedron,baxter1983tetrahedron,bazhanovsergeev2006tetrahedron}.
present_status: Status as of 12 November 2026: broad nontrivial existence was proved before the 1983 lecture (E); any additional unstated restriction remains unassessable (F).
literal_correctness: A broad assertion of nonexistence or continuing openness is historically incorrect by the lecture date; an unstated narrower question is indeterminate.
worth: Historical correction is substantive; no new broad existence problem remains.

title: Odd–even orthogonal Grassmannian identification
statement: For a nondegenerate hyperplane \(H\) in a complex quadratic space \(V\) of dimension \(2r+2\), prove that \(W\mapsto W\cap H\) identifies either component of \(\operatorname{OG}(r+1,V)\) with \(\operatorname{OG}(r,H)\).
status: Solved classical exercise. Each isotropic r-plane has two maximal extensions, one in each component. No exact earlier occurrence was identified in the supplied index.

title: Computing Ext from the trivial real mixed Hodge structure
statement: For a finite-dimensional real mixed Hodge structure \(M\), prove the quotient formula for \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb R(0),M)\) and the vanishing \(\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathbb R(0),M)=0\), \(i>1\), as stated in item 1983-630.10.
status: Solved exercise; follows from the two-term real mixed-Hodge mapping complex. No exact earlier problem occurrence was identified in the supplied cumulative index.

title: Joint critical block-magnetization limits
statement: For the critical planar nearest-neighbour Ising model, do the jointly rescaled block sums \(L^{-15/8}\sum_{x/L\in B_j}\sigma_x\) converge to a nontrivial limiting random field, with a consistent convention for lattice amplitude?
status: Closed for the nearest-neighbour planar model by Camia, Garban and Newman (2012 preprint; 2015 journal). The general universality question is separately indexed as GP-1983-91.

title: Universality of the planar critical bulk magnetization field
statement: For zero-field, translation-invariant, square-symmetric, finite-range ferromagnetic pair interactions on \(\mathbb Z^2\) with connected interaction graph, establish the critical bulk magnetization-field limit and its identification with the nearest-neighbour field after a model-dependent multiplicative normalization. The notebook does not specify this class; it is an explicit editorial reconstruction.
status: Partially developed (C). Nearest-neighbour field convergence is established. Verified 2025 results treat boundary correlations under weak perturbations. A September 2026 weak-perturbation bulk preprint was located but its primary text could not be opened; it is an unverified lead, not evidence for a new theorem. No verified result found in this run covering the stated arbitrary-strength family. This chapter proves only conditional covariance scaling from uniform two-point asymptotics.

title: Characteristic numbers without derivatives of a measurable metric
statement: Construct characteristic-number information on an oriented compact Lipschitz or quasiconformal manifold from sufficiently bounded measurable metric/conformal data, without assuming a classical curvature tensor. Distinguish global index formulas from local characteristic-cycle formulas.
status: Developed: Teleman (1983) and Sullivan--Teleman (1983) already supply the signature-index and rational-Pontryagin framework before the report; Connes--Sullivan--Teleman (1994, preprint 1993) provide later local quasiconformal constructions. The literal phrase 'curvature of every measurable metric' is not established.

title: Differentiability and energy of directional slice areas
statement: For measurable \(E\subset\mathbb R^3\) of finite volume, determine the regularity of its plane-slice area \(S_\theta(t)\) and the exact normalized spherical average of \(\int|S_\theta'(t)|^2dt\).
status: Closed as a classical Radon--Plancherel consequence: \(S_\theta\in H^1(\mathbb R)\) for almost every direction and the normalized spherical average equals \(2\pi|E|\). The chapter gives a full finite-measure proof and a separate ball check. The earlier occurrence has no problem ID and does not unambiguously specify the same averaging.

title: Scope of a Laurent-series criterion for algebraic complete integrability
statement: Does a polynomial Hamiltonian system with a full \((n-1)\)-parameter Laurent family at a fixed movable pole necessarily admit compact abelian completion of generic invariant manifolds? Here \(n\) is phase-space dimension.
status: The count-only implication is false. The chapter's explicit polynomial example \(H=pq^2\) has the required Laurent family and, after a canonical linear change, poles in both coordinates, while generic energy curves have rational function field and projective genus zero. This does not refute ordinary Liouville integrability or a criterion with stronger global hypotheses.

title: Multiplicative Poisson tensors on a vector group are linear
statement: For a finite-dimensional real vector group \((V,+)\), show that a smooth multiplicative Poisson tensor is linear in the base point and that its Jacobi identity is equivalent to a Lie bracket on \(V^*\).
status: Closed: multiplicativity gives \(\pi(x+y)=\pi(x)+\pi(y)\), and smooth additivity implies linearity. Evaluating Jacobi on linear coordinate functions gives the dual Lie-algebra Jacobi identity. This is the notebook's exercise, already within Drinfeld's 1983 framework.
